title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook - Operations Guidelines
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response processes, runbook structure, postmortem expectations, rotation policy, game day guidance, and templates for status page and customer communications. The goal is to minimize user impact, restore service quickly and safely, and learn from incidents to reduce recurrence. This playbook applies to all production-facing services and infra managed by engineering, platform, and SRE teams.

Incident Severity & SLOs

- Sev 0 (P0): Full production outage or data corruption affecting >50% of customers or critical path. Pager immediately. Target detection-to-ack < 5m; mitigation < 60m where possible.
- Sev 1 (P1): Service degradation with major customer impact (API error rate >5% or latency >3x SLO). Pager. Mitigation target < 4 hours.
- Sev 2 (P2): Partial degradation or single-customer impact requiring engineering attention. Email + on-call Slack alert.
- Sev 3 (P3): Low-impact issues, operational tasks, or planned maintenance. Handled by regular triage.

Service SLO examples (refer to service-specific SLO docs):
- Text generation API: 99.9% availability, p99 latency < 350ms for short requests (<=128 tokens)
- Embeddings endpoint: 99.95% availability, p99 latency < 150ms

Detection & Pager Thresholds

- Alerts originate from monitoring (Prometheus + Alertmanager) or external alarms (status-page, external probe).
- Standard pager triggers: sustained error rate >1% for 5m, 5xx spike >1m, p99 latency crossing threshold for 5m, queue/backpressure >80% for 3m.
- Noise reduction: use dedup windows, labels, and smart routing; avoid paging for a single transient spike unless escalation path indicates otherwise.

Incident Lifecycle (High-level)

1. Detect & Triage
   - Alert fires, Alertmanager routes to on-call rotation.
   - On-call acknowledges within 5 minutes. Record initial diagnosis in the incident channel.
2. Mobilize
   - Create an incident Slack channel (#incident-<service>-YYYYMMDD) and a running doc (Confluence incident page).
   - Assign roles: Incident Lead (IL), Communications Lead (Comms), Tech Lead, Scribe. See Roles section.
3. Mitigate
   - Apply short-term mitigations to protect customers (circuit breakers, rollback, failover to model variant). Prioritize safety over permanence.
   - Track mitigation steps and decision rationale in the running doc.
4. Stabilize & Restore
   - Move from mitigation to root cause investigation. Validate recovery with canary traffic and synthetic checks.
5. Post-incident
   - Create a postmortem within 72 hours (see Postmortem section), assign owners for action items, and schedule follow-up review.

Roles & Responsibilities

- Incident Lead (IL): Owns incident orchestration, decisions on customer impact, and declaring severity transitions.
- Tech Lead: Drives technical diagnosis and mitigation actions.
- Communications Lead: Authors status updates for internal and external audiences and coordinates with Customer Success.
- Scribe: Logs timeline, decisions, and evidence in the running doc.
- Secondary/Support: Additional engineers, infra, and product contacts as needed.

Rotation & Escalation Policy

- Primary on-call rotation: weekly cadence for service owners; pager duty shared across SRE and service teams.
- Escalation path: primary -> secondary (team) after 15 minutes -> SRE lead after 30 minutes -> Engineering Director if unresolved after 2 hours.
- Time off & handoffs: On-call owner must declare planned absences in the rotation calendar and ensure a documented handoff with outstanding issues.

Runbooks & Playbook Structure

Each service must maintain a runbook in the service folder with the following sections:
- Summary & service owner contact
- Key SLOs and alerting thresholds
- Quick triage checklist (health checks, dependency map, immediate mitigations)
- Recovery steps (rollbacks, scaling commands, model variant failover)
- Diagnostic commands and dashboards (example commands and PromQL snippets)
- Post-incident cleanup and telemetry checks

Example quick triage checklist:
1. Confirm alert: check Alertmanager, Grafana panels, and synthetic monitor.
2. Verify scope: which customers/endpoints/regions are affected.
3. Check recent deploys/rollouts: `git log` and deploy audit.
4. Check infra: node failures, GPU OOMs, networking errors.
5. Apply safe mitigation (eg. temporarily route traffic to dedicated cluster).

Diagnostic command snippets (examples):
- kubectl get pods -n service-namespace -o wide
- prometheus query: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"service\"}[1m])) by (status)`
- redis-cli info replication

Postmortem Process & Template

Timeline and expectations:
- Create a postmortem page within 72 hours of incident mitigation.
- Postmortem must include owner, summary, timeline, root cause, contributing factors, impact, action items with owners and target dates, and follow-up verification steps.
- All postmortems classified P0/P1 require a 1:1 review with Engineering leadership within 2 weeks.

Postmortem template (to copy into Confluence):
- Title: [Postmortem] <Service> - <YYYY-MM-DD> - <Short summary>
- Summary: 2-3 sentence summary of impact and resolution
- Severity: P0/P1/P2/P3
- Timeline: concise ordered timeline with timestamps and authors
- Root Cause: clear statement of root cause
- Contributing Factors: environmental and process issues
- Action Items: (owner, description, due date, verification criteria)
- Lessons Learned: 1-3 bullet points
- Verification: Post-deploy checks and date of completion

Game Days & Preparedness

- Quarterly game days run by SRE: simulate common failure modes (region failover, model degradation, spike in requests) and validate runbooks and monitoring.
- Pre-game day checklist: update runbooks, confirm rotation coverage, create simulated workload and rollback plan.
- Post-game day: actionable findings added to backlog, owners assigned.

Status Page & Customer Communications Templates

Status page content model:
- Incident ID, Start time, Affected services, Current status (Investigating/Identified/Monitoring/Resolved), Next update ETA, Short description, Impacted customers/regions, Mitigation in place.

External status update template (short):
- Subject: [Incident] Service disruption for <service> - <short impact>
- Body: We are currently investigating an issue affecting <service>. Impact: <brief>. Current status: <Investigating/Identified/Monitoring>. Next update: <ETA>. Our team is working to restore full service and will post updates to https://status.redwood-inference.internal.

Customer comms guidance:
- For material customer impact (P0/P1) route communications through Customer Success. Provide at minimum: incident summary, ETA for next update, mitigation actions taken, and postmortem link once published.
- Avoid technical jargon in customer-facing updates; include a link to the public status page and a Confluence postmortem for deeper detail for enterprise customers.

Tools & Integrations

- Monitoring: Prometheus + Grafana + Alertmanager
- Pager: PagerDuty (primary) with Slack integration to #ops-alerts and #incident-{service}
- Status page: Statuspage.io (private pages for customers) + internal mirror page
- Incident docs: Confluence templates (postmortem and running doc templates)
- Telemetry: OpenTelemetry traces, logs in Elasticsearch, and structured metrics in Prometheus

Ownership & Contacts

- On-call scheduling and rotation management: SRE team (sre-ops@redwood.com)
- Incident review chair: Engineering Director, Operations
- Customer escalation: Customer Success escalation path (cs-esc@redwood.com)

Appendix: Quick templates and checklists

- Running doc header: Incident ID, IL, Tech Lead, Comms, Scribe, start time, severity
- Short status update cadence: every 15 minutes during active mitigation, every 1 hour while monitoring
- Post-incident verification checklist: confirm SLOs returned to normal for 48 hours, validate alerts silenced or adjusted, close action items only after verification steps pass

Related pages and references:
- SLO & Error Budget policy: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- Service runbook template: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- Security incident response: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security

If you have questions about this playbook or want to schedule a game day for your team, contact the SRE on-call rotation owners or open a ticket with the SRE team.
